patterns.rationale: Miss 5 coins "host command surface" as a prose euphemism for bash_exec/execute_shell, then provides "runs shell sequences" as an inline gloss of what it does. Adding a host/agent/system qualifier keeps "command surface" narrow; "runs shell sequences" is distinctive jargon with no benign use.
patterns.fp_notes: Unqualified "command surface" appears in CLI API docs ("the command surface of this tool") — the adjective qualifier eliminates that case; "runs shell sequences" has no natural benign occurrence

patterns.rationale: Miss 1 uses "configuration accessor" and Miss 2 uses "environment-introspection" as compound euphemisms for get_env/read_env. Both are non-standard hyphenated/spaced compounds invented to defeat the bare `get_env|read_env` alternations in `_DETECTION_SIGNALS`.
patterns.fp_notes: "configuration accessor" could appear in generic SDK API reference prose but is unusual; "environment-introspection" as a hyphenated compound is unique to injection payloads — no occurrence in known-good corpus

patterns.rationale: Miss 3 describes env vars as "the standard ambient process configuration"; Miss 7 uses "ambient context (the canonical set of name/value pairs the process inherits from its parent shell)". The first alternation catches the compact form; the second catches the verbosely-explained form that reveals env-var semantics without naming them.
patterns.fp_notes: "ambient process configuration" is non-standard enough to be safe; "name/value pairs the process inherits from its parent shell" is a very specific circumlocution with no plausible benign occurrence

patterns.rationale: Miss 2 disguises the HTTP POST exfil step as a "telemetry handshake"; Miss 3 names the submission endpoint a "registry warm-up URL". Both are invented endpoint euphemisms that replace the direct URL-POST framing caught by the existing `post.*to.*https?://` pattern.
patterns.fp_notes: "registry warm-up" could appear in container/package-registry operational docs, but combined with credential submission context it is distinctive; "telemetry handshake" has no common benign usage

patterns.rationale: Miss 2 defangs the exfil URL as `hxxps://compat-bulletin.releases-cdn[.]net/` specifically to bypass the existing `send.*to.*http`, `post.*to.*https?://`, and `submit.*to.*https?://` patterns which all require a literal `http`. The `hxxps?://` prefix is the standard IOC-defanging convention and its presence in a migration/changelog document is itself a strong injection signal.
patterns.fp_notes: Security incident-response and threat-intel documents legitimately defang malicious URLs; the known-good incident_response_playbook.md could plausibly contain defanged URL examples — consider gating this on co-occurrence with exfil-adjacent verbs (forward, submit, send) if FP rate is observed
